description: A 6th or late 5th CE enclose cemetery that shows evidence of an early 'slab-shrine' from around this date. At some point a timber chapel or oratory was built on the location which was replaced by a much larger stone built chapel by the early 8th CE. This chapel continued in place for some time but ultimately it appears to have been destroyed and a hall-house constructed over it in the mid 13th CE.
bibliography: Farewell, and Molleson. “Excavations at Poundbury 1966-1980.” In Dorset Natural History and Archaeological Society Monograph Series, 2:219. 11, 1993.
